texts.preamble: Gunji Venkataramanaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 15 October, 2025 1 Aphc010672572015 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravati [3369] (Special Original Jurisdiction) Wednesday, The Fifteenth Day Of October Two Thousand And Twenty Five Present The Honourable Sri Justice T Mallikarjuna Rao Criminal Revision Case No: 2339/2015 Between: 1. Gunji Venkataramanaiah, S/O Guraviah, Aged 40 Years, Occ: Causal Laborer, Manabolu Village, Spsr Nellore District. ...Petitioner And 1. The State Of Andhra Pradesh, through Food Safety Officer, S.P.S.R.Nellore District Rep., Rep. by Public Prosecutor, High Court at Hyderabad. ...Respondent Revision filed under Section 397/401 of CrPC praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed in support of the Criminal Revision Case, the High Court may be pleased to submit this Memorandum of Criminal Revision Case being aggrieved by the order dated 02.09.2015 passed in Crl.M.P.No.558 of 2015 in C.C.No.153 of 2013 on the file of the Addl. Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Gudur, Spsr Nellore District Ia No: 1 Of 2015(Crlrcm 2015(Crlrcmp 3629 Of 2015 Petition under Section 151 Cpc praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed in support of the petition, the High Court may be pleased to stay of all further proceedings including appearance of the petitioner in C.C.No.153 of 2013 on the file of the Addl. Judicial Magi Magistrate strate of First Class, Gudur, Spsr Nellore District, pending disposal of Crl.R.C., and to pass Counsel for the Petitioner: 1. P Narahari Babu Counsel for the Respondent: Gunji Venkataramanaiah, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 15 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116229107/ 1 1. Public Prosecutor (Ap) The Court made the following Order
texts.facts: 2. When the matter was taken up for hearing, none appeared on behalf of the petitioner / accused.
texts.arguments: 3. Sri K. Sandeep, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent / State, contends that as per E-courts report, Calendar Case No.153 of 2013, wherein the order dated 02.09.2015 in Crl.M.P.No.558 of 2015 was passed, was finally disposed of by the Trial Court, resulting in the acquittal of the accused on 01.10.2018. He further contends that, in view of the dismissal of the main case, the present Criminal Revision directed against the said interlocutory order no longer survives for independent adjudication and has, therefore, become infructuous.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Sri K. Sandeep, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent / State, contends that as per E-courts report, Calendar Case No.153 of 2013, wherein the order dated 02.09.2015 in Crl.M.P.No.558 of 2015 was passed, was finally disposed of by the Trial Court, resulting in the acquittal of the accused on 01.10.2018. He further contends that, in view of the dismissal of the main case, the present Criminal Revision directed against the said interlocutory order no longer survives for independent adjudication and has, therefore, become infructuous.
